hyps.why: Replacing none with conv3x3 adds a whole path, a bigger gain than swapping one op for another.
Replacing none with conv3x3 adds a new path to the output.
Replacing none with conv3x3 reconnects node 2 to the output.
Replacing none with conv3x3 adds a new feature path via node 2.
Restoring the direct edge with a conv gains much more than replacing an op that already worked.
Removing a conv3x3 on the first edge cuts off a learnable path, costing more than removing weaker ops.
Removing a conv3x3 path costs more than removing a weak op.
Downgrading a conv3x3 to pooling loses more than downgrading a weaker op.

Deleting a conv3x3 on the direct edge loses more than deleting a weaker op.
